Verdict: for all seven Forge classes (jutsu, item, bloodline, gameAsset, quest, AI, AiProfile) plus guide and badge, a same-origin Forge on the carrier can give an admin holding a canChangeContent role the full draft -> review -> edit -> publish -> delete loop with ZERO game changes, because every step is an existing procedure: hidden/published is flipped only by the whole-record <class>.update (no toggle exists anywhere except worldMap.publishSectorMap and activityStreak.toggleConfigActive), gated resolver-side by canChangeContent returning success:false at HTTP 200. Draft READS need no role for 6 of the 7 Forge classes (public get/getAllNames; getAll honours client hidden:true) - only guide, sageMode lists, evolutions and sectorMap gate drafts on role, so 'hidden' is page-level confidentiality only (Behaviour-proven: committed captures return hidden:true quest bodies). Unhide gates exist for jutsu (appearAnimation+appearSfx), item (WEAPON/battle CONSUMABLE same rule) and quest (sceneCharacters); hiding jutsu/item force-unequips owners. AI has no lifecycle flag: 'publish' = inArena/inShrines/quest or placement references, and every AI is listed to everyone. Native audit: actionLog with server-computed diffs on update/delete for jutsu/item/bloodline/quest/gameAsset/ai/badge/guide/sageMode, never on create/clone; readable per record via public logs.getContentChanges ONLY for LOG_TYPES (ai, badge, bloodline, guide, item, jutsu, ...) - quest, gameAsset and sageMode history is written but unreachable through the API, so Forge captures are the only history there. content_backups is a whole-table prod->dev SQL sync (4 types, admin roles), not restore. Preview: public detail pages 404 hidden rows; only the guide editor has a real preview tab; Forge must self-render (ItemWithEffects is user-context free; quest/objective rendering needs a live tracker and must be re-implemented). Role discovery without credential material: profile.getPublicUser {own userId from window.Clerk.user.id} (one public budget unit) or profile.getUser (protected, unlimited, whole profile). Rate limits: every list/point read an admin queue would poll is publicProcedure 60/60s per path per user shared with the carrier page; protected reads are unlimited. Forge today: registry covers CRUD+publish for the 7 classes but has no delete/clone callers, refuses paged getAll lists (no queue), lacks logs.getContentChanges, relations/evolutions/scene-asset reads and a role pre-check; guide is entirely post-pin (forces a pin move, which the drift reader shows is contract-neutral for the existing 43 paths); badge/sageMode/skillTree/sectorMap/mapAsset/mapTerrain/overworldAi/towerDefense/rankedSeason/activityStreak/raidThreshold/itemVariant/reskins are staff-managed classes with no Forge coverage, most with NO native audit log. rows.publish_path: No publish flag, but two real lifecycle controls, both heavier than the row previously implied. (b) END: endSeason (pvprank.ts:269-292) calls endRankedSeason (pvprank.ts:807-859), which resets rankedLp and rankedStreak for EVERY user with LP > 0 and inserts a rankedUserRewards row for each of them, then sets ended:true and overwrites endDate with now. It is irreversible through the API. rows.what_visibility_means: Variants are player-purchasable skins of an item. Source-proven (NOT inferred) for the inventory surface: fetchUserItemsWithVariants drops any userItem whose item.hidden is true (item.ts:3128-3142), so hiding the parent removes its variants from /items. But hidden is NOT enforced at the API: getItemVariants (item.ts:982-990), purchaseVariant (1124-1204), consumeVariantToken (1289-1392) and fetchVariantOwnership (3175-3200) never read item.hidden, so any signed-in user can enumerate a hidden item's variants and, if they still own a copy of the item, unlock one by direct tRPC call. Unlocks persist per-user forever on userItemVariant even after every copy of the item is gone (comment at item.ts:3175-3186).
rows.review_read_path: item.getItemVariants {itemId} - protectedProcedure, NO role check, NO ratelimitMiddleware, mcp:false (item.ts:982-990). rows.lifecycle_field: TWO tables, TWO status vocabularies (the original row conflated them). historicalAvatar {id, avatar, avatarLight, createdAt, userId, replicateId, status varchar default 'started', done bool default false} and historicalSoundEffect {id, url, relationId, userId, replicateId, secondsTotal, prompt, negativePrompt, status varchar default 'started', done bool default false} - free varchar, no enum (app/drizzle/schema.ts historicalAvatar / historicalSoundEffect blocks @tnr-src (head 36c5873b); both blocks byte-identical at the Forge pin 345d18ac). STAFF content images are the only rows written status 'content-success' + done true (openai.ts:95-96), and that value is what the daily-cap query counts (openai.ts:36-37). A user's OWN generated avatar is status 'success' (avatar.ts:64-65), and EVERY historicalSoundEffect row - generated or uploaded - is status 'success' (audio.ts:89-90), so there is NO 'content-success' marker on the sound side at all: content sounds are distinguished only by relationId.
rows.what_visibility_means: There is no hidden/published flag; 'visibility' is (a) the URL being pasted into a content record's image/sound field and (b) the per-relation gallery. The two galleries are keyed DIFFERENTLY: openai.createImg stores the content record id in the historicalAvatar.userId column (openai.ts:94 'userId: input.relationId'), so the image gallery is a userId lookup being used as a relation lookup, while historicalSoundEffect has a real relationId column and audio.generate/audioSfxUploader set it (audio.ts:85-91; core.ts:201-221). Both galleries are readable by ANY authenticated user for ANY relation id - no role gate (avatar.ts:74-106; audio.ts:38-71). Role gates exist only on WRITE: a 'content-success' avatar row can be selected or deleted only by a caller with canChangeContent, and that gate fires regardless of ownership (avatar.ts:119-124 updateAvatar guard, 159-164 deleteAvatar guard - the original row cited 121/161 as if both were the delete guard).
rows.review_read_path: avatar.getHistoricalAvatars {relationId nullish, limit 1-100 nullish, cursor nullish} protectedProcedure, NOT rate-limited, no role gate, offset paging, filters done=true AND avatar IS NOT NULL, desc(id) (avatar.ts:74-106 @tnr-src (head 36c5873b)); audio.getHistorical {relationId optional, limit 1-100, cursor} protectedProcedure, same shape, filters done=true AND url IS NOT NULL (audio.ts:38-71 @tnr-src (head 36c5873b)). Both are documented in committed evidence at the task pin (skills/building-tnr-content/data/45f_DATA_procedures.json:379-419, source_drop bdec2883) - the original row's 'avatar router not read' was an avoidable hole, and it is the decisive cell: the image gallery IS avatar.getHistoricalAvatars, not an unread unknown.
rows.full_record_read: the list read IS the full record read: getHistoricalAvatars returns whole historicalAvatar rows (avatar/avatarLight/status/done/createdAt/userId) and audio.getHistorical does select() * on historicalSoundEffect (prompt/negativePrompt/secondsTotal included), so a Forge queue could capture prompt provenance for sounds. No per-id getter exists for either table.
rows.edit_path: FOUR writers. (1) generativeAi.createImg (protected; canChangeContent) inserts one 'content-success' row per returned url (openai.ts:30-100); role miss THROWS TRPCError UNAUTHORIZED (openai.ts:43-45 via serverError = new TRPCError, trpc.ts:227-232), and the cap THROWS TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when the count of ALL staff 'content-success'+done rows created in the last day exceeds 100 (openai.ts:34-51 - global across staff, counted in IMAGES not calls, and the '>100' test means the 101st blocks). (2) audio.generate (protected; canChangeContent) returns errorResponse success:false on a role miss - a DIFFERENT shape from createImg - and has no cap (audio.ts:17-36). (3) uploadthing audioSfxUploader (64KB) / audioMusicUploader (4MB) take .input({relationId}) behind adminMiddleware = canChangeContent and INSERT a historicalSoundEffect row on completion (core.ts:201-242). (4) uploadthing imageUploader (512KB) behind avatarMiddleware = any non-banned logged-in user, NO role check, capped at >50 historicalAvatar rows owned by the caller's own userId in the last day (core.ts:62-94); it inserts NO historicalAvatar row, so uploaded images never enter a gallery, while uploaded sounds do. Cross-cutting moderation/serverData risk: CC-06.
rows.publish_path: n/a (the URL is copied into the content record by the subsequent <class>.update; avatar.updateAvatar with a non-'user' ContentType performs no DB write on the content record - it only backfills avatarLight and returns the url for the form, avatar.ts:126-143).
rows.delete_path: avatar.deleteAvatar {avatar: number} (protected; canChangeContent for 'content-success' rows) - avatar.ts:145-170. It deletes the DB row ONLY: no UTApi.deleteFiles call, so the CDN object survives and any content record already pointing at that url keeps rendering. historicalSoundEffect has NO delete procedure anywhere in the router (audio.ts has exactly generate + getHistorical), so a bad generated sound can only be orphaned, never removed.

rows.content_class: gameSetting - 6 whitelisted event-gain multipliers + 8 DMG_* combat-formula rows (value is a double, schema.ts:3907-3918) - plus global tavern, which is NOT a gameSetting at all but the isEnabled flag on the conversation row titled 'Global' (misc.ts:185-209). Runtime knobs.
rows.lifecycle_field: n/a - no hidden/published flag. The only lifecycle is the gameSetting.time expiry on event-gain boosts: getGameSettingBoost counts a boost as active only while secondsLeft>0 and value>0 (gamesettings.ts:251-261), and days:0 writes an already-expired boost, which is the only way to clear one (misc.ts:229-234, validators/misc.ts:14).
rows.what_visibility_means: two different ownerships, not one: (a) direct runtime balance knobs - event gain multipliers and the live damage formula every battle resolves with (fetchDmgConfig, gamesettings.ts:268-302); (b) global tavern is a chat/moderation availability switch consumed by the tavern page (app/tavern/page.tsx:44-45) and rendered in profile/edit (page.tsx:2879-2898), not a balance knob. Reads are unauthenticated for all three, so none of this is confidential.
rows.review_read_path: all three reads are unauthenticated publicProcedure: misc.getSetting {name} (misc.ts:167-175; reads ANY setting name, including machine-owned timers/counters), misc.getDmgConfig (misc.ts:237-243 -> fetchDmgConfig, gamesettings.ts:268-302, inserts defaults for missing rows), misc.getGlobalTavernEnabled (misc.ts:176-184, defaults true when the conversation row is absent). publicProcedure carries ratelimitMiddleware (trpc.ts:201-203), so these share the 60-per-60s per path+user budget with the carrier page (CC-02).
rows.full_record_read: misc.getSetting returns the whole gameSetting row {id,name,time,value} - value is a double column (schema.ts:3913), so fractional DMG values (curve 1.6, amplitude 0.75, advantage_min 0.01) are not truncated. getDmgConfig returns a derived 8-field object, not rows. The tavern read exposes only a boolean, never the conversation record.
rows.edit_path: three protected, resolver-gated, whole-value mutations: setEventGameSetting canModifyEventGains (misc.ts:219-236), restricted by changeSettingSchema to 6 setting names (trainingGainMultiplier, regenGainMultiplier, battleExpMultiplier, missionExpMultiplier, jutsuExpMultiplier, itemExpMultiplier), a GAME_SETTING_GAINS_MULTIPLIER enum value and days 0-31 (validators/misc.ts:4-15); setDmgConfig canModifyCombatSettings (= canChangeContent, permissions.ts:166-168) writes ALL 8 DMG_* rows in one call from confSchema (validators/combat.ts:1652-1666), misc.ts:244-269; toggleGlobalTavern canEnableGlobalTavern (misc.ts:185-209) flips conversation.isEnabled. NO generic gameSetting editor exists in the API - every other gameSetting write is machine-owned (war boosts libs/war.ts:456-466, onlineUsers profile.ts:2122, cron timers gamesettings.ts:69-204). Role miss on all three returns baseServerResponse success:false at HTTP 200 (errorResponse, trpc.ts:240-242) - no UNAUTHORIZED throw, so none trips the Forge AuthState.refuse hazard of CC-01.
rows.publish_path: n/a - a write is live immediately; an event-gain boost stays live until gameSetting.time expires.
rows.delete_path: n/a - no delete procedure. The nearest equivalents are setEventGameSetting with days:0 (expires the boost) and re-submitting defaults through setDmgConfig.

rows.audit_path: NONE (re-read at head and pin, not 'not read'): misc.ts has no actionLog import or write, so setEventGameSetting / setDmgConfig / toggleGlobalTavern record nothing about who changed a live balance knob, and no logs.getContentChanges LOG_TYPE covers gameSetting or conversation (CC-03). The base rule is not the whole rule: 32 call sites across 7 routers compose .use(ratelimitMiddleware) onto protectedProcedure (misc, towerDefense, raids, combat, comments, item, travel - all mutations; item.splitStack:1522-1524 is the canonical case), identically at head and at 345d18ac, so 'protected = unlimited' must be checked per procedure and every read below was checked individually. A trip costs movedTooFastCount+1, money*0.99, bank*0.99 then TOO_MANY_REQUESTS - at trpc.ts:161-181, NOT :121-126 as the original row cited; re-read by this verifier. Every draft-queue/list read in scope is publicProcedure, verified at BOTH head and the Forge pin: jutsu/item/bloodline/quests/gameAsset(=routers/asset.ts) .getAll/.get/.getAllNames, badge .getAll/.get, logs.getContentChanges, profile.getAllAiNames/getPublicUser/getPublicUsers. Protected, unlimited reads an admin surface would use, each confirmed to carry no composed limiter at head and pin: profile.getAi (1122/1121), ai.getAiProfile (21/20), worldMap.listSectorMaps (41)/getSectorMapById (184), activityStreak.getConfigs (622/621), raids.getQuestThresholds (471/517 - raids.ts does compose the limiter on 8 mutations, but not on this read), staff.getBackups (119/106). Paging caps, head = pin: jutsu.getAll 1000, item/bloodline/quests/gameAsset/badge 500, getPublicUsers 100 (validators/user.ts:131), getContentChanges 100. A SECOND, STRICTER SURFACE the row missed: the MCP route runs its own IP limiter and per-user limiter, both slidingWindow(30,'60 s') (app/src/app/api/mcp/[[...transport]]/route.ts:22-36, head and pin), and nearly every read above is meta({mcp:{enabled:true}}) - MCP is half the tRPC budget, not a way around it. The shared window is real and now sourced: Forge appends an overlay on carrier '/' and HomeLanding.tsx:36-44 @bdec2883 client-pushes a signed-in operator to /profile, leaving the game's React tree and its tRPC traffic mounted underneath and outside Forge's accounting (forge/src/ui/takeover.mjs:20-40); /profile's own page reads are marriage/pvpRank, but profile.getPublicUsers is an infinite query on /profile/recruit (app/src/app/profile/recruit/page.tsx:72) and the per-(path,user) key is shared across every tab the user has open, not just the carrier. Forge's local mirror: DEFAULT_MARGIN 0.5 (bucket.mjs:32), allowance = max(1, floor(60*0.5)) = 30 per path per minute (bucket.mjs:108), weighted+strict double check mirroring @upstash slidingWindowLimitScript (:115-161), write-ahead sendlog, persisted trip, never retried (:169-201); covered by forge/test/budget.test.mjs:30-104. THREE Forge limits the row omitted: (1) the mirror knows only the 43 paths in forge/src/transport/procedures.mjs (PROCEDURES, generated at 345d18ac) and procedure() THROWS on anything else (:70-74), so logs.getContentChanges, badge.*, guide.*, profile.getPublicUser(s) are not merely unthrottled - they are unrunnable through the reader until the registry is re-derived at a pin; (2) CachedReader.list() REFUSES any paged getAll (reader.mjs:76 throws unless the path matches getAllNames/getAllAiNames) - exactly the call the original implication recommended, cited but never stated; (3) a limited-path batch is capped at min(maxBatch,10,allowance) per request to bound the penalty blast radius (reader.mjs:50-55). BUILDER PRECEDENT the row missed: builder_bundle.js already performs this polling - pageAll loops jutsu.getAll at limit 100 (JLIM, not the 1000 the schema allows), up to 2000 pages, sleeping THR=2000ms between pages, and loadJutsu runs it twice, the second pass with hidden:true (builder_bundle.js:217,516-519), i.e. ~30 requests/min, exactly Forge's allowance; and getRL/postRL RETRY a detected limit (isLim: 429, or an error status with a short 'too fast|too many|rate limit|slow down|infraction' body, :263) up to 8 times with 5s..60s exponential backoff (:342,345) - the opposite of Forge's halt, and under trpc.ts:161-181 each still-limited retry is another 1% money/bank hit. rows.implication_for_forge: A polling admin queue must (a) page getAll with hidden:true at a few calls per minute per path - but Forge CANNOT do this today: CachedReader.list() throws for any path that is not getAllNames/getAllAiNames (reader.mjs:76) and PROCEDURES has no entry for logs.getContentChanges, badge.*, guide.* or profile.getPublicUser(s), which makes procedure() throw (procedures.mjs:70-74); a paged-list reader plus a pin-anchored registry extension is prerequisite work, not a tuning knob. (b) Prefer name-list snapshots + point reads over repeated full lists, and prefer the protected unlimited reads (profile.getAi, ai.getAiProfile, worldMap.*, activityStreak.getConfigs, raids.getQuestThresholds, staff.getBackups) wherever they answer the same question - but re-check each one for a composed limiter, because 32 protected procedures already carry ratelimitMiddleware. (c) Never poll faster than the shared per-(path,user) window: it is shared with every tab the user has open on the game, and the carrier's own tRPC traffic is outside Forge's accounting (takeover.mjs:20-40). (d) Keep the halt-with-countdown on TOO_MANY_REQUESTS and keep never retrying - this is a DELIBERATE divergence from the Builder, whose getRL/postRL retry a trip up to 8 times with 5-60s backoff (builder_bundle.js:342,345), which under trpc.ts:161-181 pays a fresh 1% money/bank penalty per still-limited attempt; retirement must carry the divergence knowingly, and the Builder's THR=2000ms / limit=100 / double pass with hidden:true (builder_bundle.js:217,516-519) is the concrete pacing baseline to match or beat. (e) Design for pull-on-demand or long intervals (>= 1 min), not live polling. (f) If the queue ever moves to the MCP surface it gets a stricter budget (30/60s IP AND 30/60s per user), not a bigger one. (g) A guide queue additionally requires a Forge pin move: routers/guide.ts does not exist at 345d18ac.
rows.would_need_game_change: none for the read budget itself - every constraint is client-side pacing, and the halt-on-trip behaviour already exists. Two qualifications the original row missed: a guide-backed queue needs a PIN MOVE (routers/guide.ts is head-only, absent at 345d18ac and bdec2883), not a game change; and a protected, unlimited staff list endpoint (or hidden:true on an existing protected list) would remove the constraint entirely if live polling is ever wanted.

original_row.topic: Rate limits on the read paths an admin queue would poll
original_row.finding: publicProcedure = ratelimitMiddleware + sentryMiddleware (slidingWindow(60,'60 s') per `${path}-${userId ?? userIp}`); protectedProcedure = enforceUserIsAuthed + sentryMiddleware with NO limiter (app/src/server/api/trpc.ts:121-126,201-203,220-222 @tnr-src (head 36c5873b)). Every draft-queue/list read in scope (jutsu/item/bloodline/quests/gameAsset .getAll and .get, badge/guide .getAll/.get, logs.getContentChanges, profile.getAllAiNames/getPublicUsers) is publicProcedure and shares the per-(path,user) 60/60s window with the carrier page's own tRPC traffic (Forge mounts over /profile after HomeLanding's push; forge-inventory 'rate-budget'). A trip costs the user movedTooFastCount+1, money*0.99, bank*0.99 (trpc.ts:121-126 @tnr-src (head 36c5873b); reader-cited (not re-read by this merger): 161-181). Protected reads that an admin surface would use are UNLIMITED: profile.getAi, ai.getAiProfile, worldMap.listSectorMaps/getSectorMapById, activityStreak.getConfigs, raids.getQuestThresholds, staff.getBackups (trpc.ts:220-222 @tnr-src (head 36c5873b)). Paging limits: jutsu.getAll 1000, item/bloodline/quests/gameAsset/badge getAll 500, getPublicUsers 100, getContentChanges 100 per call (routers as cited per class). Forge's local mirror keeps allowance floor(60*0.5)=30 per path per minute and never retries (forge/src/budget/bucket.mjs:1-32).
original_row.implication_for_forge: A polling admin queue must (a) use paged getAll with hidden:true at <= a few calls per minute per path, (b) prefer name-list snapshots + point reads over repeated full lists, (c) never poll faster than the shared window allows because the carrier page shares it, (d) treat TOO_MANY_REQUESTS as a halt with countdown (existing Forge behaviour). Design for pull-on-demand or long intervals (>= 1 min), not live polling.

rows.finding: The game records WHAT changed - and WHO, but only for readers who pass canSeeSecretData - for: jutsu/item/bloodline/quest/gameAsset/ai/badge/guide/sageMode updates and deletes, plus mapAsset/mapTerrain. UPDATES carry calculateContentDiff strings ['Added: {...}','Deleted: {...}','Updated: {...}'] from deep-object-diff (utils/diff.ts:11-24); DELETES do NOT - every delete writes a hand-built single string ['Deleted: <name>'] (jutsu.ts:466, item.ts:395, bloodline.ts:618, quests.ts:1035, asset.ts:234, badge.ts:144, guide.ts:153 uses title, sageMode.ts:202), so a history parser cannot assume JSON after 'Deleted:'. relatedId = record id, userId = actor; table ActionLog {id, userId, createdAt, tableName, changes json, relatedId, relatedMsg varchar(191) column 'relatedText', relatedImage varchar(191), relatedValue}; indexes userId/relatedId/tableName/createdAt (app/drizzle/schema.ts:2120-2143). ACTOR REDACTION (row-critical): logs.getContentChanges rewrites entry.userId and entry.user.username to the literal 'staff' for any caller that is anonymous or fails canSeeSecretData (logs.ts:93-101), and the username filter is silently dropped for the same callers rather than rejected (logs.ts:48-51). canChangeContent (permissions.ts:22-36) includes EVENT, HEAD_EVENT and CODER, which canSeeSecretData (permissions.ts:243-257) does NOT - so a content admin holding one of those three roles can edit content but sees no actor in its history. NOT recorded: the plain create placeholders (jutsu/item/bloodline/quests/asset/badge/guide/sageMode .create), clones (item.clone, quests.clone, profile.cloneAi), jutsu.createReskin, profile.delete (AI deletion), the entire ai.* AiProfile router (createAiProfile/updateAiProfile/toggleAiProfile write no actionLog), item variants, skillTree/folder CRUD (Discord-only, skillTree.ts:216/277/318), towerDefense, overworldAi, pvprank, activityStreak CONFIG (claimStreakDay does write tableName 'activityStreak', activityStreak.ts:574), raid thresholds, worldMap save/publish/archive. EXCEPTION to 'no creates': bloodline.createReskin DOES log (tableName 'bloodline', relatedId = base bloodline id, bloodline.ts:343). RESKIN POLLUTION: jutsu.updateReskin (jutsu.ts:1655 rejection row, :1679 success row) and bloodline.updateReskin/deleteReskin/removeBloodlineFromPool write tableName 'jutsu'/'bloodline' with relatedId = the PARENT record, and are gated by canModerateReskin = isStaffRole (ANY non-USER staff role) - so a relatedId-filtered per-record history mixes player-reskin moderation traffic, including AI-rejection entries, with admin content edits. READ PATH: logs.getContentChanges is publicProcedure {logtype: z.enum(LOG_TYPES), relatedId?, search?, username?, cursor, limit<=100} filtering actionLog.tableName==logtype (logs.ts:21-60; validators/logs.ts:4-8); it pages by offset (skip=cursor*limit, nextCursor null on a short page) and REWRITES the returned change strings, substituting every bloodlineId/villageId occurrence with '<id> - <name>' (logs.ts:104-119). LOG_TYPES = ai, badge, battleAction, bloodline, clan, guide, item, jutsu, poll, user, userjutsu, villageStructure, war (app/drizzle/constants.ts:255-270) - 'quest', 'gameAsset', 'sageMode', 'mapAsset' and 'mapTerrain' are written as tableName but NOT readable through this procedure, so those five histories exist in the DB and are unreachable through the API. It is the only generic actionLog reader; the other query.actionLog reads (jutsu JutsuLevelTransfer, bloodline swap, kage, blackmarket, skillTree) are purpose-built and expose no content history. Content updates fan out to Discord (callDiscordContent) outside development for jutsu/item/bloodline/quest/gameAsset/badge/sageMode/ai/mapAsset/mapTerrain - but NOT guide (guide.ts has no @/libs/socials import). Diff content is server-computed AFTER server rewrites (item reward_reputation preservation item.ts:490-520; sageMode setEmptyStringsToNulls + persistSageTagDuration; profile.updateAi scaleUserStats and a diff restricted to the submitted keys only, with jutsu/item id-list strings appended), so server-filled defaults show as 'Added'. PIN DRIFT: at the Forge pin 345d18ac there is no guide router at all and LOG_TYPES has 12 entries with no 'guide'; logs.ts differs from head only by an import-path reorder, and validators/logs.ts, utils/diff.ts, permissions.ts and the actionLog schema are unchanged pin-to-head.

rows.implication_for_forge: Forge Next can build a per-record 'History' panel from logs.getContentChanges (public, relatedId filter) for jutsu/item/bloodline/ai/badge with zero game change, and for guide only at head (the pin has neither the router nor the LOG_TYPES entry, so a guide history panel forces the pin move). Three constraints the panel must carry: (1) the actor column is available ONLY when the signed-in admin passes canSeeSecretData - an EVENT, HEAD_EVENT or CODER content admin gets the literal 'staff' for every row and their username filter is silently ignored, so Forge must pre-check the role and label the column 'attribution unavailable for your role' rather than imply anonymity; (2) rows returned under a jutsu/bloodline relatedId include player-reskin moderation entries written by any staff role (including AI-rejection rows), so the panel must segregate them by relatedMsg prefix; (3) delete rows carry no structured diff and the reader rewrites bloodline/village ids to 'id - name' inside the change strings, so the parser must tolerate both. Polling cost is not merely a throttle: the 60/60s window is per procedure path per identity and a breach costs the admin 1% of money and bank plus a movedTooFastCount increment (trpc.ts:121-185), so the panel must be fetch-on-open, never a poll. For quest, gameAsset, sageMode, mapAsset and mapTerrain, history is written but unreachable, so Forge must rely on its own captures (already committed - 153 quests.get and 23 gameAsset.get captures across 42 bundles in harvests/inbox) and the capture contract (with an explicit 'record absent' verdict, forge-inventory defect) is load-bearing for those classes. Creates, clones, jutsu reskin creation, AI deletion and the whole AiProfile (ai.*) router are invisible to native audit: Forge's journal is the only record of placeholder minting and of every AiProfile change. Neither builder_bundle.js nor forge/src references actionLog or getContentChanges today, so this is net-new Forge surface either way.

Forge's pre-write captures remain the only per-record rollback source, and that source is narrower than 'capture.before': a full body is stored only when the entry asks persist:'full' (default is 'summary', manifest.mjs:24-25,125), only for the seven allowlisted content point reads (gameAsset.get, jutsu.get, item.get, bloodline.get, quests.get, profile.getAi, ai.getAiProfile - captures.mjs:58-68), only when input names one id, and a body over 512 KiB is an explicit persistence FAILURE rather than a shortened body (captures.mjs:78-84; runner.mjs:617). Forge has no restore/apply-snapshot path at all, so even a full capture is evidence for a manual re-apply, not automated rollback. A Content Admin flow should therefore capture persist:'full' automatically before every update/delete on the seven classes, surface the over-ceiling failure loudly, and treat quest/gameAsset (no readable native history) as the cases where losing that capture loses the only history.

THE ONLY WRITER of inArena/inShrines anywhere in the server is profile.updateAi (profile.ts:1490-1587): no toggle exists, and profile.updateUser's updateUserSchema (validators/user.ts:19-42) does not carry the fields. updateAi is a whole-record merge of insertAiSchema (schema.ts:2578-2626 = createInsertSchema(userData) minus 14 runtime columns, non-strict so unknown keys such as a manifest's hidden:true are silently stripped - skills/building-tnr-content/references/pipeline.md:433), gated by canChangeContent at profile.ts:1516, which additionally re-scales stats (scaleUserStats, 1550), applies SET-DIFFERENCE to the jutsu/item kit (updateUserContent, 1535), writes an actionLog row tableName 'ai' (1569) and calls callDiscordContent outside development (1585) - so publishing or unpublishing an AI is audited AND publicly announced. rows.implication_for_forge: 'Publish' for an AI = one whole-record profile.updateAi setting inArena/inShrines true, or binding the AI to a quest objective, an active overworld placement, or a jutsu/item SummonTag; 'unpublish' is the reverse plus a where-used check. Three consequences for the design: (a) because updateAi is whole-record, Forge must read-merge-write the live row and cannot flip a flag in isolation - the same call re-scales stats and set-difference-syncs the kit, so an omitted jutsu/item list strips the kit (already exercised by forge/test/adversarial.test.mjs:691); (b) publish/unpublish is natively audited (actionLog tableName 'ai', readable via logs.getContentChanges logtype 'ai') and also announced to Discord (callDiscordContent, profile.ts:1585), so a 'quiet hide' is not available; (c) delete writes no audit row at all, so Forge capture is the only history for an AI deletion. A Content Admin AI row should show a containment panel (inArena, inShrines, isSummon, isEvent) plus a where-used block: quests via ai.getAiRelations (public), placements via overworldAi.getPlacementsForAi (PROTECTED and it THROWS UNAUTHORIZED rather than returning success:false, so the role pre-check must handle a thrown error here, unlike the content mutations), and - not covered by any game procedure - jutsu/item effects whose SummonTag.aiId names the AI, which Forge must discover itself from the jutsu/item contracts. Require that full check before delete. Clone needs its own guard: cloneAi carries inArena/inShrines AND aiProfileId forward, so Forge should re-point or re-create the behaviour profile before pushing rules to a clone, or it will overwrite the source AI's rules. Registry gap: forge/src/transport/procedures.mjs today has profile.cloneAi/delete/updateAi and the ai.*AiProfile calls but no ai.getAiRelations and no overworldAi.* entries, so both where-used reads are a registry expansion, not a game change. Draft AIs are never confidential: they are listed and detail-readable by anyone (getPublicUsers, getPublicUser, /username/<name>); the ELDER exclusion in getAllAiNames is a name-list quirk, not confidentiality.
rows.would_need_game_change: None for the publish/unpublish/containment loop itself - insertAiSchema already accepts inArena/inShrines/isEvent/isSummon and canChangeContent already gates it. A game change would be needed only for: (i) draft confidentiality (a hidden/draft flag on userData or an isAi listing gate on getPublicUsers/getPublicUser); (ii) a quiet hide (suppressing callDiscordContent on a containment-only edit); (iii) an audit row on profile.delete; (iv) extending ai.getAiRelations to cover jutsu/item SummonTag.aiId references and overworld placements so the where-used check is complete server-side. Note also a standing risk rather than a need: insertAiSchema does not omit role, isBanned, staffAccount or money, so the publish mutation carries a privileged-column write surface that Forge should whitelist against.
